// Reference translation of pie_list `cmp_id` (corpus/src/pie_list.c).

#[repr(C)]
pub struct Point {
    pub x: i32,
    pub y: i32,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct Record {
    pub id: i32,
    pub name: [u8; 16],
    pub pos: Point,
    pub weight: f64,
}

/// `return a->id - b->id;` The subtraction wraps, as the generated code does.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn cmp_id(a: *const Record, b: *const Record) -> i32 {
    unsafe { (*a).id.wrapping_sub((*b).id) }
}
</kraken-rust>

// Reference translation of pie_list `cmp_dist` (corpus/src/pie_list.c).

#[repr(C)]
pub struct Point {
    pub x: i32,
    pub y: i32,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct Record {
    pub id: i32,
    pub name: [u8; 16],
    pub pos: Point,
    pub weight: f64,
}

fn dist2(p: &Point) -> i32 {
    p.x.wrapping_mul(p.x).wrapping_add(p.y.wrapping_mul(p.y))
}

/// Squared distance from the origin of each record's position; returns their difference.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn cmp_dist(a: *const Record, b: *const Record) -> i32 {
    unsafe { dist2(&(*a).pos).wrapping_sub(dist2(&(*b).pos)) }
}
</kraken-rust>
<kraken-result>{"assumptions": [], "unsupported": []}</kraken-result>

// Reference translation of switch_vm `vm_run` with its helpers push, pop and vm_fail
// (corpus/src/switch_vm.c).

const STACK_MAX: usize = 32;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct Vm {
    pub stack: [i32; STACK_MAX],
    pub sp: i32,
    pub pc: u32,
    pub steps: u64,
}

mod op {
    pub const HALT: u8 = 0;
    pub const PUSH: u8 = 1;
    pub const ADD: u8 = 2;
    pub const SUB: u8 = 3;
    pub const MUL: u8 = 4;
    pub const DUP: u8 = 5;
    pub const SWAP: u8 = 6;
    pub const DROP: u8 = 7;
    pub const NEG: u8 = 8;
    pub const JNZ: u8 = 9;
    pub const DEC: u8 = 10;
    pub const PRINT: u8 = 11;
    pub const AND: u8 = 12;
    pub const OR: u8 = 13;
    pub const XOR: u8 = 14;
}

fn vm_fail(msg: &str, pc: u32) -> ! {
    eprint!("vm error at pc={pc}: {msg}\n");
    std::process::exit(42)
}

fn push(vm: &mut Vm, v: i32) {
    if vm.sp >= STACK_MAX as i32 {
        vm_fail("stack overflow", vm.pc);
    }
    vm.stack[vm.sp as usize] = v;
    vm.sp += 1;
}

fn pop(vm: &mut Vm) -> i32 {
    if vm.sp <= 0 {
        vm_fail("stack underflow", vm.pc);
    }
    vm.sp -= 1;
    vm.stack[vm.sp as usize]
}

/// Runs bytecode `code[..len]` on `vm`; returns the top of stack at HALT (0 if empty).
///
/// # Safety
/// `vm` and `code` must be valid; `code` must be readable one byte past `len` (an operand or a
/// jump target is fetched without a bounds check, as in the original).
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn vm_run(vm: *mut Vm, code: *const u8, len: u32) -> i32 {
    let vm = unsafe { &mut *vm };
    let fetch = |at: u32| unsafe { *code.add(at as usize) };
    loop {
        if vm.pc >= len {
            vm_fail("pc out of range", vm.pc);
        }
        let opcode = fetch(vm.pc);
        vm.pc = vm.pc.wrapping_add(1);
        vm.steps = vm.steps.wrapping_add(1);
        match opcode {
            op::HALT => return if vm.sp != 0 { vm.stack[(vm.sp - 1) as usize] } else { 0 },
            op::PUSH => {
                let imm = fetch(vm.pc) as i8 as i32;
                vm.pc = vm.pc.wrapping_add(1);
                push(vm, imm);
            }
            op::ADD => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a.wrapping_add(b));
            }
            op::SUB => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a.wrapping_sub(b));
            }
            op::MUL => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a.wrapping_mul(b));
            }
            op::DUP => {
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a);
                push(vm, a);
            }
            op::SWAP => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, b);
                push(vm, a);
            }
            op::DROP => {
                pop(vm);
            }
            op::NEG => {
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a.wrapping_neg());
            }
            op::JNZ => {
                let a = pop(vm);
                if a != 0 {
                    vm.pc = u32::from(fetch(vm.pc));
                } else {
                    vm.pc = vm.pc.wrapping_add(1);
                }
            }
            op::DEC => {
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a.wrapping_sub(1));
            }
            op::PRINT => {
                // The original reads stack[sp - 1] without checking sp; do the same.
                let top = unsafe { *vm.stack.as_ptr().offset(vm.sp as isize - 1) };
                print!("out: {top}\n");
            }
            op::AND => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a & b);
            }
            op::OR => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a | b);
            }
            op::XOR => {
                let b = pop(vm);
                let a = pop(vm);
                push(vm, a ^ b);
            }
            _ => vm_fail("bad opcode", vm.pc.wrapping_sub(1)),
        }
    }
}

// Reference translation of stripped_calc `evaluate` with its parser (corpus/src/stripped_calc.c):
// skip_ws, parse_number, parse_atom, parse_term, parse_expr.

struct Parser {
    p: *const u8,
    err: bool,
}

impl Parser {
    fn cur(&self) -> u8 {
        unsafe { *self.p }
    }

    fn advance(&mut self) {
        self.p = unsafe { self.p.add(1) };
    }

    fn skip_ws(&mut self) {
        // isspace in the C locale: space, \t, \n, \v, \f, \r
        while matches!(self.cur(), b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | 0x0b | 0x0c | b'\r') {
            self.advance();
        }
    }

    fn parse_number(&mut self) -> i64 {
        let mut v: i64 = 0;
        let mut any = false;
        self.skip_ws();
        while self.cur().is_ascii_digit() {
            v = v.wrapping_mul(10).wrapping_add(i64::from(self.cur() - b'0'));
            self.advance();
            any = true;
        }
        if !any {
            self.err = true;
        }
        v
    }

    fn parse_atom(&mut self) -> i64 {
        self.skip_ws();
        if self.cur() == b'(' {
            self.advance();
            let v = self.parse_expr();
            self.skip_ws();
            if self.cur() != b')' {
                self.err = true;
            } else {
                self.advance();
            }
            return v;
        }
        if self.cur() == b'-' {
            self.advance();
            return self.parse_atom().wrapping_neg();
        }
        self.parse_number()
    }

    fn parse_term(&mut self) -> i64 {
        let mut v = self.parse_atom();
        loop {
            self.skip_ws();
            let op = self.cur();
            if op != b'*' && op != b'/' && op != b'%' {
                return v;
            }
            self.advance();
            let r = self.parse_atom();
            if op == b'*' {
                v = v.wrapping_mul(r);
            } else if r == 0 {
                self.err = true;
            } else {
                // i64::MIN / -1 traps in the original (idiv); here it panics, which the
                // differential test reports as the same kind of fault.
                v = if op == b'/' { v / r } else { v % r };
            }
        }
    }

    fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> i64 {
        let mut v = self.parse_term();
        loop {
            self.skip_ws();
            let op = self.cur();
            if op != b'+' && op != b'-' {
                return v;
            }
            self.advance();
            let r = self.parse_term();
            v = if op == b'+' { v.wrapping_add(r) } else { v.wrapping_sub(r) };
        }
    }
}

/// Evaluates the expression in the NUL-terminated `text`; stores the value in `*out` and returns
/// 0, or returns -1 (leaving `*out` alone) on a syntax error or division by zero.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn evaluate(text: *const u8, out: *mut i64) -> i32 {
    let mut ps = Parser { p: text, err: false };
    let v = ps.parse_expr();
    ps.skip_ws();
    if ps.err || ps.cur() != 0 {
        return -1;
    }
    unsafe { *out = v };
    0
}
</kraken-rust>
<kraken-result>{"assumptions": [], "unsupported": []}</kraken-result>
